Yes, this must be part of Godot’s core engine because:

1. The Android editor is built as a native application, and enabling C# support requires changing how the editor itself is compiled. An asset library add-on cannot modify the engine’s build process.


2. AOT compilation must be handled at the engine level, as it affects how C# is compiled and executed on Android. This cannot be achieved through a plugin.


3. Godot already provides official .NET builds for other platforms, so it makes sense to include an official "Godot .NET (AOT) for Android" version rather than relying on third-party solutions.



Since this change affects how the editor itself is built and distributed, it must be implemented at the core level rather than as an add-on.

answers.workaround:
No, this cannot be worked around with a simple script.

The lack of C# support in the Android editor is caused by Android’s restriction on JIT compilation, which is a fundamental system-level limitation. Without AOT, C# simply does not work in the Android editor.

Currently, the only workaround is to avoid using the Android editor entirely for C# projects, which is not an acceptable solution. This proposal directly addresses the problem by making C# fully functional on Android, allowing mobile developers to use the editor as intended.

title: Use AOT compilation to enable C# support in the Android editor
